correctness.rationale: For every n>=3, proper sets induce path runs whose orders must be even for a perfect matching; disjunctive coverage holds exactly when each zero-run is at most three. Rooting at one of s selected runs gives the n/s labeled coefficient formula, and differentiating the block logarithm yields the rational function. The deficit identity d=3(k-s)+sum(3-b_i) proves all five residue formulas. The root of x^2+x^3+x^4+x^5=1 is the unique dominant simple pole, giving total-count constant one. A generic graph-distance/matching verifier independently compared every vertex subset for n=3..17 with rational coefficients; exact algebra verified support and extremal multiplicities through n=250.

value.rationale: Counting every paired-disjunctive dominating configuration on the natural cycle family is motivated by the original optimization problem and is not determined by its known minimum. The result gives a full graded polynomial and rational generating function for arbitrary n, a nontrivial five-residue quasi-polynomial of minimum-set counts, the complete attainable size spectrum, exact high-end coefficients, and a sharp total-count asymptotic with coefficient one. This is an exact natural invariant rather than an arbitrary finite instance or routine scalar substitution.
